claims.title: Magan supplies copper to Mesopotamia
claims.summary: Sumerian texts record a land called Magan, identified with Oman, as a source of copper and diorite carried by sea to the city-states of Mesopotamia.

sources.label: Ancient Oman: Archaeological Digs and Historical Discoveries in the Sultanate of Oman

claims.title: Beehive tombs and towers at Bat
claims.summary: The Bronze Age communities of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn raised monumental stone towers and dry-stone beehive tombs, later inscribed by UNESCO in 1988 as the most complete such collection in the world.

sources.label: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn

claims.title: The frankincense trade flourishes in Dhofar
claims.summary: The resin of the Boswellia sacra tree, harvested in Dhofar, became one of antiquity's great luxury goods, carried by caravan and ship from southern Arabia to the Mediterranean.

sources.label: Ancient Oman: Archaeological Digs and Historical Discoveries in the Sultanate of Oman

claims.title: Khor Rori and the incense ports
claims.summary: The port of Khor Rori (Sumhuram) and later Al-Baleed served as gateways for the export of frankincense and goods across the Indian Ocean, anchoring the Land of Frankincense.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Oman: From the copper of Magan and the frankincense roads to a seafaring empire that reached Zanzibar, reborn as a modern sultanate.", terralore.co/country/OMN/chronicle#ev-300bce-khor-rori-and-the-incense-ports, claim TL:OMN:event:300bce:khor-rori-and-the-incense-ports, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oman accepts Islam
claims.summary: According to tradition, the inhabitants of Oman embraced Islam during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad, beginning the country's long Islamic history.

sources.label: Oman: History of Oman - The Imamates

claims.title: The first Ibadi imamate
claims.summary: Around 750 CE the Ibadis established their first imamate in Oman under al-Julanda ibn Masud, an elected imam uniting temporal and religious authority and giving Oman a distinctive political identity.

sources.label: Oman: History of Oman - The Imamates

claims.title: Ibadism becomes Oman's defining school
claims.summary: The Ibadi school of Islam took root across the Omani interior, making Oman its principal home and shaping a tradition of imams chosen for learning and piety rather than heredity.

sources.label: Oman: History of Oman - The Imamates

claims.title: Albuquerque captures Muscat
claims.summary: The Portuguese under Afonso de Albuquerque stormed Muscat and other Omani coastal towns, beginning more than a century of Portuguese dominance over the coast.

sources.label: Ancient Oman: Archaeological Digs and Historical Discoveries in the Sultanate of Oman

claims.title: Rise of the Yarubid imamate
claims.summary: A member of the Yarub tribe was elected imam, founding the Yarubid dynasty that would unite Oman and lead the campaign to expel the Portuguese.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Oman: From the copper of Magan and the frankincense roads to a seafaring empire that reached Zanzibar, reborn as a modern sultanate.", terralore.co/country/OMN/chronicle#ev-1624-rise-of-the-yarubid-imamate, claim TL:OMN:event:1624:rise-of-the-yarubid-imamate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Expulsion of the Portuguese from Muscat
claims.summary: The Yarubid imams recaptured Muscat in 1650, ending Portuguese occupation of the Omani coast and launching Oman as an Indian Ocean naval power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Oman: From the copper of Magan and the frankincense roads to a seafaring empire that reached Zanzibar, reborn as a modern sultanate.", terralore.co/country/OMN/chronicle#ev-1650-expulsion-of-the-portuguese-from-muscat, claim TL:OMN:event:1650:expulsion-of-the-portuguese-from-muscat, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Persian invasion amid Yarubid civil war
claims.summary: A succession dispute fractured the Yarubid state, and the Persian ruler Nadir Shah's forces invaded and occupied parts of Oman, plunging the country into crisis.

claims.title: Ahmad bin Said founds the Al Bu Said dynasty
claims.summary: Ahmad bin Said, governor of Suhar, expelled the Persian invaders and was elected imam, founding the Al Bu Said dynasty that still rules Oman.

sources.label: Ahmad ibn Said, imam of Oman

claims.title: Treaty of Amity and Commerce with the United States
claims.summary: Said bin Sultan's government concluded a Treaty of Amity and Commerce with the United States, the first bilateral treaty between Washington and an Arab Gulf state.

sources.label: Said ibn Sultan, Omani ruler and Zanzibar sultan

claims.title: Said bin Sultan moves the capital to Zanzibar
claims.summary: Said bin Sultan transferred his capital from Muscat to Zanzibar, making the island the commercial heart of his Indian Ocean empire and the chief power in East Africa.

sources.label: Said ibn Sultan, Omani ruler and Zanzibar sultan

claims.title: Death of Said and the split of the empire
claims.summary: On Said bin Sultan's death his realm was divided between his sons, one taking Muscat and Oman and the other Zanzibar, severing the African empire from Arabia.

sources.label: Said ibn Sultan, Omani ruler and Zanzibar sultan

claims.title: Zanzibar separated from Oman
claims.summary: Following an arbitration award, Zanzibar was formally separated from Muscat and Oman as an independent sultanate, severing the African empire and its revenues for good.

sources.label: Said ibn Sultan, Omani ruler and Zanzibar sultan

claims.title: Accession of Sultan Said bin Taimur
claims.summary: Said bin Taimur came to the throne and ruled an increasingly isolated and undeveloped Oman, leaning on British support to hold the country together.

sources.label: Said ibn Taymur, sultan of Oman

claims.title: Outbreak of the Dhofar rebellion
claims.summary: An uprising began in the neglected southern province of Dhofar against Said bin Taimur's rule, growing into a Marxist-led insurgency that would dominate Omani affairs for a decade.

sources.label: Ancient Oman: Archaeological Digs and Historical Discoveries in the Sultanate of Oman

claims.title: Oil exports begin
claims.summary: Oman began exporting oil in commercial quantities, the start of the revenue that would later finance the country's modern transformation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Oman: From the copper of Magan and the frankincense roads to a seafaring empire that reached Zanzibar, reborn as a modern sultanate.", terralore.co/country/OMN/chronicle#ev-1967-oil-exports-begin, claim TL:OMN:event:1967:oil-exports-begin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: Qaboos bin Said deposed his father Said bin Taimur and became sultan, ending Oman's isolation and beginning the modernization drive known as the Renaissance.

claims.title: Defeat of the Dhofar rebellion
claims.summary: With British and Iranian support and a policy of amnesty and development, Qaboos's forces overcame the Dhofar insurgency, securing the unity of the country.

claims.summary: Sultan Qaboos issued the Basic Law, Oman's first written constitution, defining the organs and guiding principles of the state.
